# sdio_host: generation prompt

```text
Create a new SystemVerilog IP block for the FPGA Cores 4 U digital IP library.
```

## 1. Identity

- Module name: `sdio_host_top` (IP directory `sdio_host`)
- Library category: `peripherals`
- Location: `ip/peripherals/sdio_host/`
- One-line purpose: SD / SDIO host controller (single-block transfers, 1-bit or 4-bit data bus, SD mode).
- Version: 1.0.0

## 2. Context

- Where it is used: standalone library block.
- Existing IP to reuse (do not duplicate):

| Module | From | Description |
|---|---|---|

## 3. Parameters

| Name | Default | Meaning / legal range |
|---|---|---|
| `BUF_BYTES` | `512` | - |

Reject illegal values at elaboration with `$error` inside a generate block.

## 4. Clocks, resets and clock-domain crossings

- Clocks: `aclk`.
- Resets: `aresetn`.
- Clock and reset behaviour, and any clock-domain crossing, as described in section 6.
- Every clock domain: name, frequency, source, the logic on it. Every reset: one per domain, synchronous active low inside the domain, entering the domain only through a reset synchroniser (asynchronous assertion, synchronous release); reset sequencing between domains has a single, documented source.
- Every clock, reset and signal boundary uses a clock-domain crossing technique, listed in the file header. Never sample another domain's signal directly; never pass a multi-bit value through independent single-bit synchronisers. Example techniques:

| Technique | Use for | Library module |
|-----------|---------|----------------|
| Two- (or more) flop synchroniser (`async_reg`) | single slow level signal (enable, status, IRQ level) | `bit_sync` |
| Pulse synchroniser (toggle, sync, edge detect) | one-clock event / pulse | `pulse_sync`, `toggle_sync` |
| Reset synchroniser (async assert, sync release) | a reset entering a clock domain | `reset_sync`, `reset_ctrl` |
| Asynchronous FIFO with Gray-coded pointers | data stream at any rate ratio | `async_fifo`, `axis_async_bridge` |
| Request / acknowledge handshake (2- or 4-phase) | occasional multi-bit word, register access | `axi4_lite_cdc`, `clock_domain_bridge` |
| Multi-cycle path formulation (hold data, sync a qualifier) | multi-bit value that changes rarely | `cdc_sync_bit` + held register |
| Gray-code counter | counter value read in another domain | inside `async_fifo` |
| Glitch-free clock gate / mux | stopping or switching a clock | device BUFGCE / BUFGMUX, `clk_gen` enables |
| Related clocks from one PLL (fixed phase) | serializers, e.g. 10:1 TMDS, 7:1 LVDS | `clk_gen` outputs of one oscillator |

- Constrain every crossing (false path / max delay on the synchroniser's first flop) and document it.

## 5. Interfaces

- **s_axil_*** - AXI4-Lite slave, address [7:0], 32-bit data.
- **s_axis_t*** - AXI4-Stream slave (input), tdata [7:0].
- **m_axis_t*** - AXI4-Stream master (output), tdata [7:0], tlast.

| Port | Dir | Width | Group | Built when | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aclk` | input | 1 | - | - | - |
| `aresetn` | input | 1 | - | - | - |
| `sd_clk_o` | output | 1 | - | - | - |
| `cmd_o` | output | 1 | - | - | - |
| `cmd_oe_o` | output | 1 | - | - | - |
| `cmd_i` | input | 1 | - | - | - |
| `dat_o` | output | [3:0] | - | - | - |
| `dat_oe_o` | output | [3:0] | - | - | - |
| `dat_i` | input | [3:0] | - | - | - |
| `irq_o` | output | 1 | - | - | - |

Back-pressure on every stream: honour tready, never drop data unless section 6 says so; valid must not depend combinationally on ready.

AXI4-Lite / register map: as listed in the behaviour text in section 6. Out-of-range accesses return SLVERR (or DECERR where stated).

## 6. Function

Implement exactly this behaviour (from the reference design's specification):

```text
SD / SDIO host controller (single-block transfers, 1-bit or
4-bit data bus, SD mode). The registers (cfg_* / sts_*
ports; sdio_host_top.sv is the block with its AXI4-Lite register map,
src/include/sdio_host_regs.sv, ID "SDIO" / VERSION / DATE at 0x00-0x08)
issue one command at a time - 0x10 CMD (write starts it): index[5:0],
response[7:6] (0 none, 1 short 48 bit, 2 long 136 bit), data
direction[9:8] (0 none, 1 read block, 2 write block), no_crc_check[10]
(for R3/R7-style responses without valid CRC7); 0x14 ARG; 0x18..0x24
RESP0..RESP3 (short response argument in RESP0, long response 127..0
in RESP3..RESP0); 0x28 STATUS (bit0 busy, bit1 cmd_done, bit2
dat_done, bit3 cmd_timeout, bit4 cmd_crc_err, bit5 dat_crc_err, bit6
dat_timeout, bit7 buf_err; write 1 to clear bits 1-7); 0x2C CTRL
(half_period[15:0] in system clocks, minimum 1, bus4[16], clk_en[17]);
0x30 BLKSIZE (bytes, 1..BUF_BYTES); 0x34 TIMEOUT (SD clocks for
data/busy timeout); 0x38 IRQ_EN (bit n enables STATUS bit n+1 for
irq_o). Data - a block buffer of BUF_BYTES bytes
decouples the free-running SD clock from AXI-Stream: for a write, fill
the buffer through s_axis (BLKSIZE bytes, only accepted while idle)
and then issue the write command; a read block is verified (CRC16 per
data line) and only then streamed out on m_axis (tlast on the final
byte), a block with a CRC error is discarded. The command engine
appends CRC7, checks the CRC7 of short responses, waits up to 80 SD
clocks for a response, and for writes handles the CRC status token and
the busy signal. SD signals - sd_clk_o (half period = CTRL.half_period
system clocks), cmd_o/cmd_oe_o/cmd_i and dat_o/dat_oe_o/dat_i[3:0] are
separate outputs and inputs (connect to tri-state buffers at the top
level, external pull-ups on CMD/DAT); outputs change on the falling
edge of sd_clk_o, inputs are double-registered and sampled on rising
edges. Clock - aclk; SD clock runs only while CTRL.clk_en=1 and must
be running for a command to progress (initialisation at 400 kHz needs
a half period of 125 at 100 MHz). Not supported - multi-block
transfers, SPI mode, UHS-I / 1.8 V, DMA. Reset - synchronous aresetn,
sd_clk low, all lines released. Latency - about 2*half_period system
clocks per SD clock; a 512 byte block takes about 1100 SD clocks in
4-bit mode and 4200 in 1-bit mode. Errors - cmd_timeout, cmd_crc_err,
dat_crc_err (also for a bad end bit or write CRC status), dat_timeout,
buf_err (bad BLKSIZE, write without a full buffer, or a command while
busy).

sdio_host with its AXI4-Lite register interface, the block
designs and testbenches instantiate: the register map sdio_host_regs
(u_regs, src/include/sdio_host_regs.sv, ID "SDIO", VERSION and DATE at
0x00-0x08, the registers from 0x10) and the logic sdio_host (u_core,
src/sdio_host.sv), joined by their register ports (cfg_* to the logic,
sts_* back). Generated by ip/scripts/regmap_gen.py from
sdio_host_regs.json and the ports of sdio_host: regenerate after changing
either. Clock - aclk. Reset - synchronous active low aresetn.
```

Describe and handle the edge cases, error recovery, latency and configuration-change rules stated above; where the text is silent, choose the safe option and document it in the file header.

### Register map (from `sdio_host_regs.json`)

| Offset | Name | Access | Reset | Description | Fields |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0x00 | ID | RO | "SDIO" | IP identifier, 4 ASCII characters (first in [31:24]) | - |
| 0x04 | VERSION | RO | - | version, ASCII "d.dd" (+0.01 at every source update) | - |
| 0x08 | DATE | RO | - | date of the last source update, BCD mm/dd/yyyy | - |
| 0x10 | CMD | RW | 0 | a write starts the command; reads back the last one | INDEX[5:0] command index; RESP[7:6] response: 0 none, 1 short 48 bit, 2 long 136 bit; DIR[9:8] data: 0 none, 1 read block, 2 write block; NO_CRC[10] 1: no CRC7 check of the response (R3 / R7) |
| 0x14 | ARG | RW | 0 | command argument | - |
| 0x18 + 4 i (i < 4) | RESP | RO | 0 | response: short in RESP[0], long 127..0 in RESP[3]..RESP[0] | - |
| 0x28 | STATUS | CMD | 0 | status; write 1 to clear bits 1-7 | BUSY[0] command or data in progress; CMD_DONE[1] command finished; DAT_DONE[2] data block finished; CMD_TIMEOUT[3] no response; CMD_CRC_ERR[4] response CRC7 error; DAT_CRC_ERR[5] data CRC16, end bit or CRC status error; DAT_TIMEOUT[6] data or busy timeout; BUF_ERR[7] bad BLKSIZE, write without a full buffer, or command while busy |
| 0x2C | CTRL | RW | 2 | SD clock and bus | HALF_PERIOD[15:0] SD clock half period in system clocks (minimum 1); BUS4[16] 1: 4-bit data bus; CLK_EN[17] 1: SD clock running |
| 0x30 | BLKSIZE | RW | 512 | block size in bytes (1..BUF_BYTES) | - |
| 0x34 | TIMEOUT | RW | 100000 | data / busy timeout in SD clocks | - |
| 0x38 | IRQ_EN | RW | 0 | bit n enables STATUS bit n + 1 for irq_o | - |

The block is generated, not hand-written: write the JSON above and run `python3 ip/scripts/regmap_gen.py ip/peripherals/sdio_host/src/include/sdio_host_regs.json`, which also emits the C header and Markdown documentation. Extend the generator rather than editing its output.


## 7. Implementation constraints

- Synthesizable SystemVerilog-2012, technology independent (no vendor primitives; infer RAM and DSP).
- Must work in iverilog 12+ (`-g2012`), Verilator lint (`-Wall`, no UNOPTFLAT or latches) and Yosys.
- iverilog limits: declare before use; no enum ternaries without casts; no `break`; no arrays of queues; no `wait` on function calls; no declarations inside nested loop bodies of static initial blocks.
- No combinational path from a ready input back to a ready output; hoist scratch variables (no latches); split control and data `always_ff` blocks.
- One statement per line (`a <= b; c <= d;` is two lines; `if (x) y <= 1; else y <= 0;` is four).
- Instantiations: one parameter per line in `#( ... )` and one port per line, closing with `) u_name (` and `);` at the instance's indentation; a port-group macro is one port on its own line.
- Check with `python3 ip/scripts/sv_format.py --check <files>` (it can also rewrite: whitespace only, token-checked).
- Resources: report the Yosys utilisation; keep it in line with similar library blocks.

## 9. Guidelines

Follow the design guidelines in `ip/docs/DESIGN_GUIDELINES.md` (complete rules; this prompt wins where it sets a value explicitly). In short:

- Synthesizable, technology-independent SystemVerilog-2012; behavioural models behind `` `ifdef SYNTHESIS `` black boxes; iverilog / Verilator / Yosys clean.
- Layout: one statement per line; one parameter and one port per line in instantiations; two-space indent; a comment on every port.
- Naming: `lower_snake_case` modules and files, `u_` instances, `g_` generate blocks, `UPPER_CASE` parameters, `_i` / `_o` / `_n` / `_t` port suffixes, `s_axis_` / `m_axis_` / `s_axil_` buses.
- Clocks and resets per domain, every crossing through a CDC technique (see the clocks section).
- AXI4-Stream data with back-pressure, AXI4-Lite control (ID / INFO registers, SLVERR out of range), defined switch-over points for configuration changes.
- Self-checking testbench with an independent model, named `test_<what>` tasks in `tb/tests/<name>_tests.sv`, gaps and back-pressure, a mutation check, 100 % code coverage.
- Diagrams: module and instance names, arrows from output to input, no crossing lines, every clock and reset domain labelled.

Guidelines file: `ip/docs/DESIGN_GUIDELINES.md`   (replace with your own guidelines file if needed)

## 12. Verification requirements

The reference testbench checks the following; the new testbench must cover at least the same:

```text
Self-checking testbench for sdio_host with a behavioral SD
card model (CMD0, CMD2 long response, CMD8, CMD13, CMD17 block read,
CMD24 block write, R3 response, four 512 byte blocks, 1-bit and 4-bit
buses, CRC7/CRC16 generation and checking). Tests command/response of
all types, block write then read back in 1-bit and 4-bit mode,
streamed data and tlast, corrupted response CRC, corrupted read data
CRC (block must be discarded), write CRC error status token, response
timeout, data timeout, buf_err cases (command while busy, write
without data, bad block size), interrupt output and the W1C status.
Prints TEST PASSED on success.
The test tasks are in tests/sdio_host_tests.sv (`included).
```

Also: an independent reference model (not a copy of the RTL); random input gaps and output back-pressure on every stream; register readback; edge cases; a mutation check (break one rule, show the testbench fails).

Every simulation script names the tests it can run: `ip/scripts/run_sim.sh sdio_host --list-tests` prints them (and every run prints them at its start). Put each test in its own `test_<what>` task in `tb/tests/<name>_tests.sv`, listed with a one-line description in that file's header.

Tests of the reference design (the new design must provide at least these):

| Testbench | Test | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `sdio_host_tb` | `test_id_block` | ID "SDIO", VERSION ("d.dd"), DATE (BCD mm/dd/yyyy) at 0x00-0x08, read only (SLVERR); 0x0C reads 0 (register offsets from bfm.base = 0x10, the map after the ID block) |
| `sdio_host_tb` | `test_setup` | 1-bit bus, SD clock on |
| `sdio_host_tb` | `test_commands` | Commands and responses (none, short, long R2, no CRC, timeout, CRC error) |
| `sdio_host_tb` | `test_block_1bit` | Block write and read back, 1-bit bus |
| `sdio_host_tb` | `test_block_4bit` | Block write and read back, 4-bit bus |
| `sdio_host_tb` | `test_read_crc_err` | A read block with a data CRC error is discarded |
| `sdio_host_tb` | `test_write_crc_err` | Write CRC status error |
| `sdio_host_tb` | `test_data_timeout` | Data timeout |
| `sdio_host_tb` | `test_buf_err` | BUF_ERR cases (bad BLKSIZE, short buffer, command while busy) |
| `sdio_host_tb` | `test_irq` | irq_o from enabled STATUS bits |

Code coverage (`make cov`, `ip/scripts/run_cov.sh`): every target is 100 % by default. A target may be lowered only here, per metric, with the reason; every item left uncovered is listed with its justification (unreachable by design, tied-off parameter, ...).

| Metric | Target |
|--------|--------|
| Line (statement) | 100 % |
| Branch (if / case arms, ternaries) | 100 % |
| Expression / condition | 100 % |
| Toggle (every bit 0->1 and 1->0) | 100 % |
| FSM state and transition | 100 % |
| Functional (a cover point / cover property per requirement, mode and corner) | 100 % |
| Assertions (every SVA property exercised, none failing) | 100 % |

Pass criteria: `make -C peripherals/sdio_host test` passes, every coverage target met, Verilator lint clean, `sv_format.py --check` clean, `make synth` passes.
